knowledgePattern: Count compressed periods before summing their signed integrals

hints.title: Use one compressed period
hints.body: Think first about f(kx) for a positive integer k. Determine the width of one period and how the horizontal scaling changes its signed area.
hints.recap: A horizontal compression scales strip widths and their signed integral by the same factor.
hints.pitfall: The integral over one compressed period is different from the integral over a whole unit interval.
hints.pause: Calculate the area factor and count the periods in a unit interval.

recall.reminder: A horizontal compression scales strip widths and their signed integral by the same factor.

hints.title: Count complete blocks
hints.body: Use the integer nature of rr and of the upper integration limit to divide each integral into complete repeated blocks.
hints.recap: An identity with a positive period also holds after any integer multiple of that period.
hints.pitfall: Do not confuse the summation index with the exponentiated input multiplier.
hints.pause: Find a general summand, then sum over the given index range.

recall.reminder: An identity with a positive period also holds after any integer multiple of that period.

solution:
1. For a positive integer k, the graph of f(kx) compresses each period of f to width 1/k. Its signed integral over one compressed period is 1/k times the given unit-period integral, hence 1/k.

2. There are k such periods in [0,1], so ∫01f(kx)dx=1. For the rth summand, k=rr is a positive integer, and [0,r] consists of r unit intervals, each with the same signed integral 1.

3. Therefore the rth summand equals r. The requested sum is 1+2+⋯+100=100·101/2=5050. Answer D.
